title.narrative: Support for partnership and strengthening of the response to the threat of the spread of HIV/AIDS in Tunisia

description.narrative:
Although Tunisia is a low HIV prevalence country (less than 1 %) and the epidemic is stable over time, certain factors may increase the vulnerability of the population to the infection and should encourage increased vigilance. These factors fall into two categories: external factors, such as the geographic situation of the country, and factors due to socioeconomic changes. The national response has been from the first appearance of HIV/AIDS in 1985 immediate and rapid, and is essentially funded by the State, which in particular provides universal coverage of antiretroviral drugs free of charge. However the analysis of the current situation and the response as organized to date has shown that despite the efforts in terms of treatment and care and Most-at Risk Populations important gaps prevail. 

With the help of the Global Fund the current Program consolidates the country’s achievement in HIV/AIDS control in line with the strategic plan 2006-2010 , ensuring that the epidemiological situation remains stable and will strengthen the response , in particular by establishing a second-generation surveillance system, setting up centers providing anonymous free testing and by reducing vulnerability of Most-at –Risk-Populations (young people who have dropped out of school, commercial sex workers, men having sex with men, injecting drug users and by advocating the involvement of a broad range of national and international stakeholders, including e.g. key ministries, universities, private sector, development partners,
non-governmental organizations, people living with HIV/AIDS and their families.

UNOPS offers support for the partnership and strengthening of the response to the threat of the spread of HIV/AIDS in Tunisia and the grand recipient, the National Office for Family and Population (Office National de la famille et de la population).
